ledger.note: The Ligures, a people of north-western Italy with a culturally distinct Bronze Age area of Piedmont, Liguria, western Lombardy and western Emilia. The page gives no founding date, so 500 is a placeholder before the first dated event (page silent); the Etruscans are 'the one stable eastern boundary in the literary tradition'.

ledger.note: 238 BC: Rome's first Ligurian campaign. '238 BC Ti. Sempronius Gracchus fought them'; triumphs follow in 236 (Lentulus) and 233 (Q. Fabius Maximus). The zone is the researcher's reading of 'north-western Italy' and the Apuani page says the 238-233 campaigns were 'possibly partly directed against the Apuani'.

ledger.note: c. 177 BC: Rome plants Luna and Lucca. 'c. 177 BC: Colonies of Luna and Lucca secured the southern frontier.' The page names the colonies, not their land; the discs are the researcher's reading, and the Apuani page says nothing of confiscation.

ledger.note: 155 BC: Rome's last Ligurian campaign. '155 BC M. Claudius Marcellus drove back the Apuani for the last time'; the Apuani page: 'Ligurian resistance was not finally broken until 155 BC'. The Ligures page gives no single end date: by the mid-2nd century the Italian Ligures were 'subdued and drawn into the Roman economy'.

wars.outcome: Roman victory after a long series of campaigns: 238-233 (Gracchus, Lentulus, Fabius), 201 peace with the Ingauni, 187 offensive and 185-181 Ingauni campaigns, the deportation of the Apuani to Samnium in 180, the Statielli enslaved in 173, and Marcellus's last campaign in 155.
wars.note: Dates from the Ligures table and the Apuani and Ingauni pages. The 187 offensive of Flaminius and Lepidus, Philippus's 4,000 men lost at the Saltus Marcius in 186, and the 180 surrender of about 12,000 Apuani (about 40,000 deported to the ager Taurasinus in Samnium) are on the Apuani page.

notes: New state, not in Cliopatria (the eu-03 scope). The Ligures were tribes, not one state: type 'state' is chosen so that roman-republic's Ligures contest (238-155) has a land to blend with, but a gap-filler may split Ingauni, Apuani, Statielli, Taurini, and the transalpine Salyes (Entremont, 123) into their own dossiers. No capital is given by any page. Start 500 is a placeholder (page silent). Not drawn because the pages do not place them: the Friniates (subdued 187, Emilian slope), the Statielli (173, 'Carystus, unlocated'), the ager Ligustinus et Gallicus, Genoa (an ally of Rome from 218, destroyed by Mago and rebuilt in 203). roman-republic's ledger has contest_start/contest_end with 'Ligures' (-238, -155) but no gain; its counterpart string should become the slug ligures, and a matching 155 gain is missing there. Wikidata id left null. Family 'italy' is a registry key.
